The target and the roll

Strikes each turn, in order

Everything lives in the address bar, so 🔗 Copy Link shares it and a reload keeps it; nothing is saved.
The Strike, degree of success, multiple attack penalty, cover, off-guard, deadly, and fatal rules are summarized in the Gazette's own words from Pathfinder Player Core (Paizo Inc.), used under the ORC License.

How hit chance and damage work in Pathfinder 2e

A Strike hits when the d20 plus your attack modifier equals or beats the target's AC, and it's a critical hit when it beats the AC by 10 or more. A natural 20 makes the result one degree better and a natural 1 one degree worse. So a natural 20 isn't an automatic hit (against an AC 20 or more above the roll it only turns a critical failure into a failure), and your crit chance climbs with your bonus: every +1 moves both the hit and the crit chance by 5%.

A critical hit doubles all the damage, the modifiers and precision damage included, so 1d8 + 4 averages 8.5 on a hit and 17 on a crit. Damage per turn is each Strike's chance to hit times its average, plus its chance to crit times the crit average, added up.

The multiple attack penalty

Your second attack in a turn takes −5 and every one after that −10; an agile weapon takes −4 and −8, and a ranger with the Flurry edge −3 and −6 (−2 and −4 when agile). The penalty belongs to the weapon making that Strike, so a longsword then an agile dagger takes the dagger's −4. The results list every Strike on its own line, so you can see what a third Strike at −10 is really worth before you spend the action on it rather than on a Step, Raise a Shield, or a spell.

Fortune, misfortune, and bonuses

Fortune rolls twice and keeps the higher, misfortune the lower. Like 5e's advantage, the effect is biggest in the middle: a Strike that needs an 11 goes from 50% to 75% with fortune, and down to 25% with misfortune. Bless gives a +1 status bonus to attack rolls and heroism +1 to +3; status bonuses don't stack, so set the highest. A circumstance bonus or an item bonus is already part of your attack modifier.

What the options cover

  • Off-guard takes 2 off the target's AC: flanked, prone, grabbed, or caught by a feint.
  • Cover: lesser +1 AC, standard +2, greater +4.
  • Deadly adds a die of its size on a crit, after doubling: two dice once the weapon rolls three damage dice (greater striking) and three at four dice (major striking). Fatal turns the weapon's dice into its size on a crit and adds one more. The calculator takes the first dice in the damage as the weapon's dice, so write them first: 2d8 + 4 + 1d6, not 1d6 + 2d8 + 4.
  • Extra damage on every hit is for a rogue's sneak attack against an off-guard target or any damage that lands with each hit; on the first hit it's for a once-a-round bonus such as a ranger's Precision edge. Both double on a crit. Persistent and splash damage aren't counted.
  • Times is how many Strikes you make with that weapon in a turn, in row order. Set a row to 0 to keep it listed without counting it.

Works with

Look up a creature's AC in the Bestiary or the conditions that change it, build the fight in the Encounter Builder, and run it in the Initiative Tracker or from the GM Screen.
